questions.q: Why is the Data Import Wizard generally not a serious option for a full migration of real size or complexity?
options: It can't delete records, only runs one import job at a time, and doesn't support every object
It cannot be used by System Administrators
It requires a paid license that most orgs don't have
It only works with XML files, never CSV
questions.explain: The Wizard is built for small, simple, one-off loads into a limited set of supported objects. Its real limitations for migration work are that it can't delete records and runs only one job at a time.

questions.q: In Data Loader, what does checking the "Use Bulk API" option actually do?
options: It disables Upsert as an available operation
It removes the need for any object permissions
It raises the batch size ceiling from the standard 200 up to 10,000, by handing the job to Bulk API under the hood
It converts the job into a Data Import Wizard job automatically
questions.explain: Standard Data Loader batches cap at 200 records; checking "Use Bulk API" raises that to up to 10,000 by submitting the job to Bulk API 2.0 rather than using a separate mechanism.

questions.q: Which of these is a real, documented Bulk API 2.0 limit according to this lesson?
options: A maximum of 50 records per internal batch
A maximum of 10,000 records loaded per 24-hour period
A maximum of 5 ingest jobs per org, ever
A maximum of 150 MB per ingest job's file size
questions.explain: Bulk API 2.0's documented limits include a 150 MB per-job file size cap, auto-chunked internal batches of up to 10,000 records, and a 150,000,000-record ceiling per rolling 24-hour period — not 10,000 records per day, and not a 50-record batch cap.

questions.q: What does Hard Delete in Data Loader require beyond ordinary Delete access?
options: Nothing extra — Delete access alone is sufficient
The "Bulk API Hard Delete" system permission
A Full sandbox environment specifically
An active Duplicate Rule on the target object
questions.explain: Hard Delete bypasses the Recycle Bin entirely, making deleted records immediately eligible for permanent removal, which is why it requires the separate "Bulk API Hard Delete" system permission in addition to normal Delete access.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when does the extra cost of a third-party ETL/iPaaS tool (like MuleSoft, Jitterbit, or Informatica) tend to actually be worth it?
options: When transformation complexity or ongoing integration needs justify it, not just one-time migration volume alone
For every migration, regardless of size or complexity
Only when the object being migrated isn't supported by the Data Import Wizard
Never — Salesforce's own tools are always sufficient for any migration
questions.explain: ETL/iPaaS tools add a staging layer, visual transformation design, and orchestration at real licensing and setup cost — a cost this lesson says is usually only justified by transformation complexity or ongoing integration needs, not raw one-time volume alone.
